effects: The signer sends exactly `assets` EURC to the vault (enter: safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets)).
New gteurcb shares are minted to `onBehalf`. The amount is previewDeposit(assets), taken from the vault's share price at execution time.
Before the deposit, accrueInterest mints fee shares to the fee recipients, which dilutes the share price used for this deposit.
formats.shown: Deposit <amount> EURC for <onBehalf>. Fields show the exact EURC amount, the share ticker gteurcb, and the address that gets the shares.

findings.title: deposit: the number of gteurcb shares received is not shown, only the ticker.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol deposit: `uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets);` is computed from storage. The descriptor field 'Share ticker' is a raw constant "gteurcb" with no amount. Case 0: the signer got 475.13 gteurcb, and the reader wrote 'amount not shown'.
findings.fix: No calldata holds the share amount. You could relabel the field 'You receive: gteurcb vault shares' so it reads as the asset received.

cases.notes: 482.116605 EURC out matches the screen. The shares in have the right ticker and recipient, but their amount is not shown (spec limitation).

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: gteurcb shares equal to previewWithdraw(assets) (rounded up) are burned from `onBehalf`.
Exactly `assets` EURC is sent from the vault to `receiver`.
When the signer is not `onBehalf`, the signer's share allowance from `onBehalf` drops by the number of shares burned, unless it is unlimited.
The vault may pull liquidity from its liquidity adapter to pay out. This does not change what the signer gets.
formats.shown: Withdraw exactly <assets> EURC to <receiver>, with the Owner whose shares are burned.

findings.title: withdraw: the number of gteurcb shares burned is not shown and is not bounded by calldata.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol withdraw: `uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets);` then exit → deleteShares(onBehalf, shares). Case 2: the signer burned 1971.0146 gteurcb, which no field shows. The reader wrote 'exact share amount not shown'.
findings.fix: Not fixable from calldata. You could name the share token in a label, e.g. 'Owner (gteurcb burned from)'.

cases.notes: 2000 EURC in to the signer is shown exactly. The 1971.01 gteurcb burned has no amount on screen.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: EURC equal to previewRedeem(shares) (rounded down) is sent from the vault to `receiver`. There is no minimum-out parameter.
When the signer is not `onBehalf`, the signer's share allowance from `onBehalf` drops by `shares`, unless it is unlimited.
formats.shown: Redeem <shares> gteurcb to <receiver>, with the Owner. Nothing says which asset or how much the receiver gets.

findings.title: redeem: the screen never names EURC as the asset received; the mint format shows it as a constant.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol exit: `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets);`. The redeem fields are only shares, receiver and onBehalf, while mint has a field with value "$.metadata.constants.underlyingToken"Ticker. Case 3: the signer received 5002.657703 EURC, and the reader wrote 'Unknown amount of the vault's underlying asset (likely a euro-based token)'.
findings.fix: Add a field {label: 'Receive asset', value: '$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker'} and use an interpolatedIntent like 'Redeem {#.shares} for EURC to {#.receiver}'.

findings.title: redeem: the EURC amount received comes from the share price and has no minimum bound.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol redeem: `uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares);`. Nothing in calldata bounds it. Case 3: 5002.657703 EURC was received and is not on screen.
findings.fix: Not fixable in the descriptor. The function has no minAssets parameter.

cases.notes: The 4922.59 gteurcb burned is shown exactly. The EURC received is shown with neither asset nor amount; the reader only guessed it was a euro token.

effects: The signer pays previewMint(shares) EURC (rounded up) to the vault. The amount is set by the share price at execution and has no maximum bound.
formats.shown: Mint <shares> gteurcb for <onBehalf>. A 'Deposit asset' field says EURC without an amount.

findings.title: mint: the intent never says the signer pays EURC; it reads like a free mint.
findings.evidence: Descriptor mint interpolatedIntent "Mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}". The only hint of payment is the raw constant field 'Deposit asset: EURC'. VaultV2.sol enter: safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets). Case 1: the signer paid 0.903602 EURC.
findings.fix: Use intent 'Deposit EURC' and interpolatedIntent 'Deposit EURC to mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}'.

findings.title: mint: the EURC amount taken from the signer is not shown and has no maximum in calldata.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol mint: `uint256 assets = previewMint(shares);` is computed from storage and rounded up. Case 1: 0.903602 EURC left the signer, and the screen shows only 'EURC'. The reader wrote 'How much EURC will be taken. The screen shows only the share amount.'
findings.fix: Not fixable in the descriptor. The function has no maxAssets parameter. Signers who want an exact spend should use deposit.

cases.notes: EURC out is named but has no amount. The 0.9 shares going to 0xdead (signer null) is shown correctly as the onBehalf address.

redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver,.worst: redeem: the screen never names EURC as the asset received; the mint format shows it as a constant.

mint(uint256 shares, address onBehalf).worst: mint: the intent never says the signer pays EURC; it reads like a free mint.

summary.worst: redeem: the screen never names EURC as the asset received; the mint format shows it as a constant.
